title: One meaning for 'the advisor', and an advisor answer is shown to be real
why: Your worry, Oct 26: the advisor setup is delicate, and your Mac sessions seem to report an advisor review that may not exist.
note: Checked at claude-settings 149f4bc5, Oct 26. Three things are called advisor: (1) Claude Code's built-in advisor, on through settings.json advisorModel: opus, a stronger model a session consults on its own (exact behaviour in the app not checked); (2) the terminal advisor, a session named advisor-xx started by start-advisor.ps1 from C:\advisor, Windows only, no Mac launcher; (3) this cloud project, which answers only you. Rule questions-ask-advisor-first and the report label 'Decided by the advisor' mean (2) only, but nothing checks that a listed answer came from a real SendMessage to advisor-xx; and any session in a folder starting 'advisor' (such as a normal session opened in the advisor repo) gets an advisor- name and would be taken for it (known gap in decision advisor-answers-questions). On the Mac, (2) never runs, so a 'Decided by the advisor' item there likely came from (1) or was made up (unverified: no Mac report seen). Last live check of (2): Oct 23. Plan: first read one Mac report that cites the advisor; then (a) rename the label and rule to name only the advisor- session and say the built-in advisor is a second opinion, never a decision; (b) the report gate refuses a 'Decided by the advisor' item when the session sent no SendMessage to advisor-xx. Ruling needed from you on keeping (2) at all. Docs, Oct 26 (code.claude.com/docs/en/advisor): the built-in advisor is a server tool; Claude decides when to call it (before committing to an approach, on a recurring error, before declaring done); it sees only that session's full conversation, no files or other sessions; the transcript shows an 'Advising' line that ends 'Reviewed', 'Declined' or 'Unavailable', guidance under Ctrl+O; subagents inherit it. On since Oct 17 (#500, advisorModel opus). That 'Reviewed' line is the likely source of the Mac 'advisor review' you saw: real, automatic, from the built-in tool. Your question, Oct 26: why not use it instead of the terminal advisor. Advisor take: different jobs. The built-in one second-guesses a session's own work from its own context; the terminal one holds your plan and rulings from outside and answers questions so they do not wait on you. Decision card sent: keep both, or retire the terminal advisor. Your ruling, Oct 26: retire the terminal advisor once cloud building (c52) runs; until then it keeps answering local goal sessions.
ask: No brief yet. Needs one Mac report that cites the advisor, then your pick on keeping the terminal advisor.
